category_title: Dominant students with high levels of physical and verbal aggression
student_description: This student exhibits high levels of reactive physical and verbal aggression, easily triggered by direct instructions or peer comments. They uniquely require indirect, non-confrontational approaches to emotional regulation, specifically building empathy through external subjects like animal welfare and collaborative group work without explicit moralizing.

criteria.criterion_name: Neutrality on Moral and Social Skills
criteria.rationale: Explicitly teaching social skills or compassion triggers resistance, so the student must internalize these values indirectly.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must explicitly avoid direct instruction on behavior, ethics, or social skills, maintaining a neutral stance on moralizing.

criteria.rationale: Observing external situations of suffering (like animal cruelty) naturally elicits the compassionate feelings this student needs to reduce aggressive impulses.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must incorporate visual media (e.g., documentaries, videos) focused on external empathy-building topics like animal welfare.

criteria.rationale: Working continuously in mixed-skill groups helps the student organically develop peer tolerance and focus, reducing fights over time.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must structure the learning environment around continuous, small, mixed-peer collaborative groups.
